analysis:
The change is test-only: it adds endOfPromptBoundaryRequiresDensePagedSSD in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Vision/QwenVLMTargetExtractionTests.swift (head lines ~335-366). It asserts that EngineV2Factory.demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens returns the store's minEffectiveTokens only for a dense Qwen model on a paged backend with an actual paged SSD store. It returns nil for MoE, contiguous, nil store and a contiguous-fixture store. It also asserts that demandedCaptureBoundaryMinimumTokens stays nil for dense.

I examined the base text, including the existing hybrid and complete-checkpoint slot bridge tests, and the patch excerpt. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the tail of the new test and the production-side implementation of demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens are not visible. No production code is changed in this batch.

Relevant threat: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007). The test constrains the new end-of-prompt checkpoint capture to the encrypted paged SSD store. That is consistent with the SSD tier being the sole production cache tier and with the existing floor behavior, so it does not widen the at-rest surface. The existing tests still pin the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch (cacheEnabled false yields no store and no capability).

No security regression is identified in the supplied evidence. Open question for integration: if the production change in EngineV2Factory+Production.swift (not supplied) adds a new capture boundary, it should keep the existing per-donation gate (adoption bound + 1,024-token benefit floor), HMAC lookup naming, the 30-minute TTL and the authenticated cacheSalt scoping. Those controls are not visible in this batch.
